name: Growth Track
description: Progressive interview-style problems: two pointers, sliding window, stacks, binary search, intervals, graphs, and DP. Harder than warm-up drills — built to stretch you.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.prompt: Merge two sorted lists into one sorted list in O(n+m) time without using sort(). Return a new list.

problems.title: 3Sum Closest
problems.prompt: Given a list of integers nums and an integer target, find three integers whose sum is closest to target. Return that sum. You may assume each input has exactly one solution.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.prompt: Given a list of non-negative integers height where height[i] is the height of a vertical line at index i, find two lines that form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum area.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.prompt: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
problems.solution:
def trap(height):
    if not height:
        return 0
    lo, hi = 0, len(height) - 1
    left_max = height[lo]
    right_max = height[hi]
    water = 0
    while lo < hi:
        if left_max < right_max:
            lo += 1
            left_max = max(left_max, height[lo])
            water += left_max - height[lo]
        else:
            hi -= 1
            right_max = max(right_max, height[hi])
            water += right_max - height[hi]
    return water

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.prompt: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.prompt: Given strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. If no such window exists, return an empty string.

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.prompt: Given two strings s1 and s2, return True if s1 is a permutation of a substring of s2 (same character counts), otherwise False.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.prompt: Given a list of temperatures temperatures, return a list answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after the ith day to get a warmer temperature. If there is no future day, answer[i] = 0.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.prompt: Given a list of integers heights representing the bar height of a histogram with unit width, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
problems.solution:
def largest_rectangle_area(heights):
    stack = []
    best = 0
    extended = list(heights) + [0]
    for i, h in enumerate(extended):
        while stack and extended[stack[-1]] > h:
            height = extended[stack.pop()]
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            width = i - left - 1
            best = max(best, height * width)
        stack.append(i)
    return best

problems.title: Car Fleet
problems.prompt: There are n cars going to the same destination along a one-lane road. target is the distance. position[i] and speed[i] describe car i. A car cannot pass a slower car ahead; it forms a fleet. Return how many fleets arrive at the destination.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.prompt: Given a rotated sorted list of distinct integers nums and an integer target, return the index of target or -1. Aim for O(log n).

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.prompt: Given piles[i] banana piles and h hours, Koko eats at speed k (piles per hour from one pile, remainder takes another hour). Return the minimum integer k such that she can finish all piles within h hours.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.prompt: Given two sorted lists nums1 and nums2, return the median of the two sorted lists. Overall run time should be O(log(m+n)).

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.prompt: Given a list of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return a list of non-overlapping intervals sorted by start.

problems.title: Insert Interval
problems.prompt: Given a list of non-overlapping intervals sorted by start and a new interval, insert new_interval into the list and merge if necessary. Return the result sorted by start.
problems.solution:
def insert_interval(intervals, new_interval):
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(intervals)
    while i < n and intervals[i][1] < new_interval[0]:
        result.append(intervals[i])
        i += 1
    while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= new_interval[1]:
        new_interval[0] = min(new_interval[0], intervals[i][0])
        new_interval[1] = max(new_interval[1], intervals[i][1])
        i += 1
    result.append(new_interval)
    while i < n:
        result.append(intervals[i])
        i += 1
    return result

problems.title: Meeting Rooms II
problems.prompt: Given a list of meeting time intervals [start, end), return the minimum number of conference rooms required.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.prompt: Given an m x n binary grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.prompt: There are num_courses courses labeled 0..num_courses-1. prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means b must be taken before a. Return True if you can finish all courses (no cycle).
problems.solution:
from collections import defaultdict, deque

def can_finish(num_courses, prerequisites):
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    indeg = [0] * num_courses
    for a, b in prerequisites:
        graph[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    q = deque([i for i in range(num_courses) if indeg[i] == 0])
    taken = 0
    while q:
        node = q.popleft()
        taken += 1
        for nxt in graph[node]:
            indeg[nxt] -= 1
            if indeg[nxt] == 0:
                q.append(nxt)
    return taken == num_courses

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.prompt: Given an m x n matrix heights, water can flow to a cell if the neighbor height is <= current. Return coordinates [r, c] from which water can flow to both the Pacific (top/left) and Atlantic (bottom/right) oceans, sorted by row then column.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.prompt: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.prompt: Given coin denominations coins and an integer amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make amount. If it cannot be made, return -1. You have infinite coins of each denomination.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.prompt: Given an integer list nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

problems.title: Word Break
problems.prompt: Given a string s and a list of words wordDict, return True if s can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words. Words may be reused.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.prompt: Given a list of non-negative integers nums where nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i, return True if you can reach the last index starting from index 0.

problems.title: Gas Station
problems.prompt: There are n gas stations in a circle. gas[i] is gas at station i; cost[i] is cost to travel to the next. Return the starting station index if you can travel around once, otherwise -1. If a solution exists it is unique.

problems.title: Hand of Straights
problems.prompt: Given a list of integers hand and an integer group_size, return True if the hand can be rearranged into groups of group_size consecutive cards. group_size must divide the hand length.

problems.title: Partition Labels
problems.prompt: Given a string s of lowercase letters, partition it into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part, and return the sizes of the parts.

problems.title: Design LRU Cache (function API)
problems.prompt: Simulate an LRU cache with capacity. Given a list of operations and capacity, return the list of get results (None/null for misses). Operations are ['put', key, value] or ['get', key].

problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.prompt: Given a list of tokens in Reverse Polish Notation, evaluate the expression and return the integer result. Division truncates toward zero.
